questions.stem: What is the difference between irradiation and contamination?

options.text: Irradiation only applies to gamma rays; contamination applies to alpha and beta
Irradiation is always more dangerous than contamination
Irradiation is exposure to radiation from an external source; contamination is having radioactive material on or inside you
There is no difference; they mean the same thing

questions.explanation: Irradiation means being exposed to radiation from an external source (it stops when the source is removed). Contamination means radioactive material is on or inside you, so exposure continues until it is removed or decays.

questions.stem: Why is contamination generally considered more dangerous than irradiation?

options.text: Because contamination only involves gamma rays
Because contamination produces stronger radiation
Because contamination cannot be easily stopped; the source stays with you and continues to irradiate
Because contamination always leads to cancer

questions.explanation: Contamination is more dangerous because the radioactive material remains on or inside the body, continuing to irradiate tissues until it is removed or decays. With irradiation, exposure stops as soon as the external source is removed.

questions.stem: How does ionising radiation cause harm to living cells?

options.text: By ionising atoms in molecules, especially damaging DNA
By heating the cells until they burst
By making the cells radioactive
By dissolving cell membranes

questions.explanation: Radiation strips electrons from atoms (ionisation), creating ions and free radicals that damage molecules, especially DNA. This can cause cell death, mutations, or cancer.

questions.stem: Which safety precaution reduces exposure to radiation by handling sources at a distance?

options.text: Wearing a lab coat
Using long-handled tongs
Washing hands after the experiment
Turning off the lights

questions.explanation: Long-handled tongs are used to keep radioactive sources at a distance from the body. Increasing the distance from a source significantly reduces the radiation dose received.

questions.stem: Which type of radiation poses the greatest danger if a radioactive source is swallowed?

options.text: Beta, because it can travel further inside the body
All types are equally dangerous inside the body
Alpha, because it is the most ionising and would cause maximum damage to internal tissues
Gamma, because it is the most penetrating

questions.explanation: Alpha particles are the most ionising, meaning they cause the most damage per unit distance. Inside the body they cannot escape and deposit all their energy in nearby cells, causing severe localised damage.

options.text: Low-level radiation that is always present in the environment from natural and artificial sources
Radiation from nuclear power stations only
Radiation that only exists underground
Radiation produced by mobile phones

questions.explanation: Background radiation is the low-level ionising radiation present everywhere from natural sources (rocks, soil, cosmic rays, radon gas, food) and some artificial sources (medical procedures, nuclear fallout).

questions.stem: Which is the largest source of background radiation for most people in the UK?

options.text: Nuclear power stations
Radon gas from the ground
Cosmic rays from space
Medical X-rays

questions.explanation: Radon gas, which seeps from rocks (especially granite), is the largest single source of background radiation for most people in the UK, accounting for about half of the average annual dose.
